data.name: Nicolas
data.gender_notes: Nicolas is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek 'Nikolaos', meaning 'victory of the people'. In the Bible, there were several figures named Nicolas, including a disciple of Jesus in the New Testament and a leader in the early Christian church. The name Nicolas carries the meaning “Victory of the People” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Nicolas usually hope their child will grow to embody victory of the people and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the triumph of the human spirit over adversity and the power of community to overcome challenges. It is a name that embodies courage, determination, and resilience.
data.etymology: Nicolas belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victory of the People.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nicolas total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: ניקולאס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ניקולאס הוא שם נוצרי הנגזר מהמילה היוונית Νικόλαος, המורכב מניצחון ועם, ומשמעותו ניצחון העם, השם מוזכר בברית החדשה ונחשב לשם מקובל במסורת הנוצרית

in_greek.name: Νικόλαος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Νικόλαος είναι χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από τις λέξεις νίκη και λαός, και σημαίνει νίκη του λαού, το όνομα αναφέρεται στην Καινή Διαθήκη και θεωρείται ένα δημοφιλές όνομα στην χριστιανική παράδοση

in_latin.name: Nicolaus
in_latin.long_meaning: Nicolaus est nomen christianum quod derivatur a verbis victoria et populus, et significat victoriam populi, nomen in Nova Testamenta mentionem habet et habetur nomen usitatum in traditione christiana

in_english.name: Nicolas
in_english.long_meaning: Nicolas is a Christian name derived from the Greek words nike and laos, meaning victory of the people, the name is mentioned in the New Testament and is considered a popular name in Christian tradition

data.cultural_impact: The name Nicolas has been popular in Western cultures and is particularly common in France, Belgium, the Netherlands, and England. In these countries, Saint Nicholas is a beloved figure whose story has been passed down through generations. He is often depicted as a joyful, rotund man with a white beard, wearing a red cape and hat. The legend of Saint Nicholas was the inspiration for the modern-day Santa Claus.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Nicolas holds deep spiritual meaning, symbolizing victory and the triumph of the Christian faith over adversity. This name reminds us of the power and strength found in the faith and love of God. It also honors the memory of Saint Nicholas, a humble servant of God who devoted his life to helping others, demonstrating the true power of kindness and generosity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nicolas means "victory of the people of God" in Greek origin. It symbolizes the triumph of the divine will over human struggles and the ultimate victory of faith. This name also embodies the spirit of generosity and kindness, reflecting the giving nature of the Christ Child symbolized by the traditional gift-bearing Santa Claus figure.

biblical_reference.note: Nicolas is mentioned as one of the seven deacons chosen by the apostles

historical_references.reference: Nicholas of Myra, also known as Saint Nicholas, was a historical Bishop of Myra (in present-day Turkey). He is known for his many miracles. The legendary account and cult of Saint Nicholas spread throughout Europe during the Middle Ages due to the Eastern Romans' profitable trade with Europe. Saint Nicholas is said to have been born in the province of Lycia, in the Roman Empire, in AD 270.
historical_references.context: Historical figure, Bishop of Myra, Legendary accounts of miracles

historical_references.reference: Nicolas Copernicus was a prominent Polish astronomer and mathematician who formulated a heliocentric model of the universe, placing the Sun at the center rather than the Earth. He published his results in 1543, a time when the geocentric model of the universe, with Earth at its center, was widely accepted by the Catholic Church.
historical_references.context: Astronomer, Mathematician, Heliocentric model of the universe

modern_usage.modern_context: In modern context, the Christian name 'Nicolas' has been associated with two distinct trends. The first trend is the 'techie' or tech-savvy individual. This is a common nickname for Nicholas in the tech industry, where it represents the idea of a knowledgeable, innovative, and skilled individual. The second trend is the association of Nicholas with 'Santa Claus'. While this is a more traditional usage, it continues to be popular in pop culture and social media, where images and memes of a tech-savvy Santa are common.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named David Nicolas in Rome, Italy credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Nicolas, which means "Victory of the People". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
